content.text: How Johnson and Johnson Found Patterns Hidden in Ablation Data?
How Johnson & Johnson used CARTONET to organize AVNRT ablation data and explore patterns across procedures

Custom analytical framework for AVNRT ablation procedures with automated data normalization, statistical analysis, and 3D visualization

content.text: Executive Summary

HumbleBeeAI developed a custom analytical framework for Johnson & Johnson to address cardiac ablation analysis in AVNRT procedures. Procedure records were difficult to align and interpret across patients; CARTONET was built to normalize the data, support statistical analysis, and provide interactive 3D views. The source reports improved consistency and analysis efficiency, but gives no numerical performance measure. This portfolio entry is based on a reviewed website snapshot, with owner approval pending.

attrs.chunkText: For Johnson and Johnson, analyzing cardiac ablation data had always been a puzzle. Each procedure generated mountains of raw files that were hard to align, normalize, and interpret. With HumbleBeeAI's custom analytical framework, J&J turned this challenge into an opportunity. The solution automated data normalization, statistical analysis, and interactive 3D visualization, transforming complex procedural data into actionable insights that drove both efficiency and smarter decision making.

HumbleBeeAI responded with AVNRT Ablation Analysis with CARTONET, a custom framework built to transform raw, scattered data into clarity.

Integrated Data Processing and Normalization: All raw XLSX and CSV files were ingested into a unified system. By using UUID identifiers and reference-based normalization anchored on His signal coordinates, every dataset was aligned to a common spatial reference. This eliminated the core obstacle of cross-patient comparison.

Automated statistical analysis: The framework computed summary statistics such as power, temperature, impedance drop, and spatial distances. Box plots, percentiles, and comparative charts made trends visible at a glance, replacing manual calculation with automated precision.

Advanced 3D Visualization: With Plotly, HumbleBeeAI built interactive 3D models and LAO and RAO projections that revealed the spatial relationships between His signals, ablation sites, and outcome categories. Users could rotate views, filter by category, and quickly turn dense data clouds into clear visual narratives.

Predictive Modeling: The system went a step further by correlating pre-ablation features with outcomes. This gave J&J early insights into predictors of procedural success and laid the foundation for more refined strategies in the future.

content.text: Context and Challenge

The project addressed a data-structure problem, not a lack of clinical data. Files for AVNRT procedures included XLSX and CSV records, while patient-specific 3D mapping coordinates differed and the tabular data could contain inconsistent categories, free-text annotations, or missing codes. As a result, cross-patient comparison depended on manual cleanup and was difficult to perform consistently. The source describes these constraints but does not quantify the number of procedures, users, or time spent in the prior workflow.

attrs.chunkText:
The challenge was not the lack of data but the lack of structure.

Data alignment was broken: Each patient's 3D mapping data used different coordinates, making cross-patient comparison nearly impossible.

Formats were inconsistent: XLSX and CSV files arrived with categorical mismatches, free-text annotations, and missing codes that required endless manual cleanup.

The scale was daunting: With multi-patient datasets growing rapidly, traditional methods were slow and unreliable.

Interpretation was difficult: Even when processed, 3D ablation data was overwhelming to visualize and compare in a way that made sense to clinical experts.

Without a streamlined solution, J&J faced long manual hours, inconsistent outputs, and missed opportunities to uncover the procedural insights that could improve patient outcomes.

As a global leader in healthcare, Johnson and Johnson is constantly searching for new ways to improve procedural outcomes and patient care. One area of focus was the analysis of cardiac ablation data from AVNRT procedures. Each case carried valuable information hidden inside electrophysiological recordings and biophysical metrics. But without a structured way to interpret this information across multiple patients, the insights remained locked away.

To unlock them, J&J needed more than spreadsheets. They needed a system that could standardize complexity, highlight patterns, and provide clear answers.

content.text: Solution and Capabilities
Data normalization for comparison

CARTONET ingested XLSX and CSV files and aligned datasets to a common spatial reference using UUID identifiers and reference-based normalization anchored on His signal coordinates. This approach was intended to make comparisons across patients possible despite differing coordinate systems.

content.text: Results and Business Impact

The source reports improved consistency through standardized formats and structured calculations, and improved analysis efficiency through automated preprocessing and analysis. It supplies no numerical measure, baseline, comparison period, or test conditions for these observations. No measured time saving, predictive validation, or effect on clinical outcomes has been provided. These reported observations are not quantified business or clinical results.

attrs.chunkText:
The results were transformative.

Efficiency skyrocketed as automated pipelines replaced manual preprocessing, cutting down time from data collection to insight generation.

Accuracy improved through standardized formats and structured calculations, making cross-patient comparisons both reliable and consistent.

Insights became actionable. Interactive visualizations and clear statistical summaries revealed patterns that were previously invisible, helping clinical experts identify outcome predictors with confidence.

The predictive framework created a foundation for long-term learning, opening doors for J&J to refine procedural strategies and advance patient care.

In short, what was once raw and chaotic became structured, interpretable, and deeply valuable.

content.text: Limitations and Next Steps

The case-study source describes data normalization, statistical analysis, interactive visualizations, and exploratory predictive correlations as part of the framework. It does not state deployment or production-availability status, and no demo link is supplied; availability beyond the described project work is therefore unknown. Predictive performance and clinical impact remain unvalidated in the supplied evidence. Owner approval of the reviewed website snapshot is pending. No further roadmap or next steps have been provided.

content.text: Conclusion

CARTONET’s documented contribution was to bring scattered AVNRT ablation files into a more consistently structured basis for analysis, with statistical summaries and interactive spatial views to support cross-patient exploration. The source reports efficiency and consistency improvements, but provides no quantified results or evidence of clinical impact.
